Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Brian, DOB: 08/08/1982, Gender: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Not recorded, Practice: Not recorded, Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal:
  - Depressive symptoms — provisional: Major depressive disorder vs Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (onset after starting new job ~2 months ago; low mood, insomnia, low energy, reduced appetite, impaired concentration, decreased libido). 
- Secondary:
  - Insomnia/sleep disturbance (difficulty sleeping; trouble getting up).
- Tertiary:
  - Possible medical contributors to mood/fatigue to be ruled out: thyroid dysfunction (history of hypothyroidism on levothyroxine), anemia; exertional dyspnea with exercise noted over months (requires medical evaluation).

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications:

Physical Symptoms:

  - Difficulty sleeping; trouble waking/“getting up” in the morning.
- Appetite:
  - Reduced appetite.

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others:
  - Denies suicidal or homicidal thoughts. No self-harm behaviors reported.
- Protective Factors:
  - Married; engaged with care; willing to follow-up; denies SI.
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self):
  - Low, based on current denial of SI/HI and help-seeking.
- Emergency Contact:
  - Not recorded.

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Family history of suicide (father). History of hypothyroidism.
- Precipitating factors: New job ~2 months ago temporally linked to onset of low mood, insomnia, fatigue.
- Perpetuating factors: Ongoing insomnia and daytime fatigue; reduced appetite; decreased libido; possible thyroid under/over-replacement or anemia; exertional dyspnea limiting activity.
- Protective factors: Marriage; insight and motivation to improve; denies SI/HI; engaged in care.
- Working understanding: Current presentation is consistent with a depressive episode vs adjustment disorder with depressed mood, potentially compounded by sleep disturbance and possible medical contributors (thyroid dysfunction, anemia). Further assessment and labs are warranted to clarify diagnosis and guide treatment.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Return to prior level of functioning.
  - Improve energy, sleep, appetite, mood, and interest/libido to support daily life and work.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Clarify diagnosis (MDD vs Adjustment disorder) and symptom severity.
  - Identify and treat contributing medical factors (thyroid control, anemia).
  - Initiate evidence-based interventions to improve mood, sleep, and functioning.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Attend in-person GP appointment and recommended blood tests.
  - Begin regular sleep schedule (consistent wake time, limit naps; wind-down routine).
  - Engage in gradual, tolerable physical activity and pleasurable activities (behavioral activation) as energy allows.
  - Communicate with spouse about support needs; consider involving partner in care if patient agrees.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Perform in-person examination.
  - Order labs: TSH and free T4; complete blood count; iron studies; vitamin B12 and folate (to assess for medical contributors consistent with DDx).
  - Consider morning total testosterone if low libido persists after initial evaluation.
  - Screen symptom severity with PHQ-9 (depression), GAD-7 (anxiety), and an insomnia measure (e.g., ISI).
  - Provide brief psychoeducation on depression, sleep hygiene, and behavioral activation; consider referral to psychotherapy (e.g., CBT/CBT-I).
  - Discuss pharmacotherapy options if criteria for MDD are met and patient is agreeable.
  - Arrange follow-up to review results and response to initial strategies.

Secondary Problem (if applicable): Insomnia/sleep disturbance
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Fall asleep more easily and feel more refreshed on waking.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Reduce sleep latency and nighttime awakenings; improve sleep quality and daytime functioning.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Keep a 1–2 week sleep diary.
  - Implement stimulus control (bed only for sleep/intimacy; get out of bed if unable to sleep after ~20 minutes).
  - Reduce late-day caffeine and maintain a consistent wake time daily.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide CBT-I resources/referral as available.
  - Review medications and substances that may affect sleep (none reported; assess at visit).
  - Reassess sleep after addressing mood and medical contributors.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: No. Topics Covered: Not recorded (to be provided at next visit: depression, sleep hygiene, role of medical conditions).
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Escalating insomnia, marked drop in appetite/weight, increasing anhedonia, persistent low energy affecting work/home, emergence of suicidal thoughts.
- Coping Strategies:
  - Sleep hygiene, behavioral activation, pacing activities, relaxation/breathing exercises, seeking support from spouse/friends, and contacting care team if symptoms worsen.

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan:
  - Yes — agreed to in-person evaluation and investigations.
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient:
  - Not recorded.
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care:
  - Not recorded.
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional):
  - Not recorded.
- Review Date:
  - Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Major depressive disorder vs Adjustment disorder with depressed mood — Likelihood: High. Justification: 2 months of low mood, insomnia, fatigue, reduced appetite, poor concentration, decreased interest/libido temporally linked to new job; denies suicidality.
- Primary insomnia/stress-related sleep disturbance — Likelihood: Medium. Justification: Difficulty sleeping since starting a new job with downstream fatigue and cognitive symptoms; may coexist with or exacerbate depression.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Formal psychiatric diagnosis not finalized; limited MSE detail; emergency contact not documented; alcohol/substance history not recorded; follow-up/review date not specified; standardized symptom scales not administered yet.
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - Morning erections: initially “not noticed recently,” later “no change” — conflict noted.
  - Thyroid history briefly misheard as hyperthyroid, then clarified to hypothyroid — conflict noted and resolved.
  - Symptom duration initially “few weeks,” later clarified to “~2 months” — resolved.
- Transcript quality notes:
  - Telehealth visit without vitals or exam; brief freeze/connection issue noted by clinician; limited detail on social/substance history.
